detailed_summary: This paper introduces 'aquaternionicity' as a new alchemical resource theory for even-dimensional qudits (d ≥ 4), based on a quaternionic structure represented by an antiunitary Θ with Θ² = -I. Alchemical resource theories are those where a nonfree state can be exactly replicated by free operations, and finitely many copies enable exact simulation of arbitrary quantum instruments. Previously, only two nontrivial examples existed: imaginarity and parity asymmetry, which exhaust the qubit case and exhibit an all-or-nothing property where any nonmaximal resource exactly simulates only free unitaries. The authors show that aquaternionicity is extremal in two senses: every pure state is alchemical, and alchemicality is maximally abundant under mixing. They prove that for any nontrivial d-dimensional resource theory and pure alchemical state g, the admissible pure-mixing set satisfies dim M_g ≤ 2d-4, with aquaternionicity saturating this bound for every pure state. Conversely, these two extremal properties characterize the quaternionic structure. A key practical consequence is that because every pure state is alchemical, the initial resource can be chosen to match known noise structure. When noisy resource states remain within a common isotropic subspace, the same free processor works exactly for all of them while returning the resource unchanged, enabling recalibration-free exact simulation, including universal quantum computation. This is realized for standard dephasing and dissipative noise, where aquaternionicity substantially outperforms imaginarity and parity asymmetry.
